topic: The Windmill Problem: A Journey through IMO Geometry
target_audience: High school students interested in advanced mathematics and competition logic.

sections.title: Introduction: The Dancing Line
lecture_lines: Start with a set of finite points in space.
A line passes through one point, called the pivot.
The line rotates clockwise around this pivot point.
It continues until it hits another point in the set.
The hit point becomes the new center of rotation.
animations: Fade in a set of 10 points (#FFFFFF) scattered randomly.
Draw a line (#00FFFF) passing through a single central point.
Rotate the line (#00FFFF) clockwise around the central pivot point.
Line hits a second point (#00FF00); both points flash.
Scale up the line and points slightly to emphasize the Dancing motion.

sections.title: Prerequisite: General Position & Rotation
lecture_lines: We assume no three points lie on one line.
This ensures the line hits only one point at once.
The line's angle determines its unique position and state.
animations: Display 3 points (#FFFFFF); move one slightly to show non-collinearity.
Show a line [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/line.svg] (#00FFFF) rotating with a circular arc (#FFFF00) indicating angle.
Highlight the pivot point [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pivot.svg] in Green (#00FF00) and label it 'Pivot'.

sections.title: Visualizing the Pivot Swap
lecture_lines: Watch as the line approaches the next point nearby.
Upon contact, the rotation axis shifts to that point.
The line's direction remains continuous during this transition.
animations: Line (#00FFFF) rotates clockwise around Point A (#00FF00).
Line (#00FFFF) hits Point B (#FF0000); rotation pauses.
Points A and B both flash in White (#FFFFFF) to signal the swap.
Line (#00FFFF) begins rotating clockwise around Point B (#FF0000).
Trace the sweep of the line with a faint Yellow trail (#FFFF00).

sections.title: The Core Invariant: Counting Sides
lecture_lines: Consider the points on each side of the line.
Color points on the left red and right blue.
As the pivot swaps, a point moves through the pivot.
Crucially, the number of points on each side stays constant.
This invariant is the key to solving the problem.
animations: Label 4 points on the left as '4' (#00FFFF) and 4 on the right as '4' (#FF00FF).
Line (#FFFFFF) rotates and swaps pivots while maintaining the count.
Flash the labels '4' and '4' to show the invariant property.

sections.title: The 180-Degree Flip
lecture_lines: Now, let the line rotate exactly 180 degrees.
The line returns to its original position in space.
However, its "left" and "right" sides have now swapped.
Points originally on the left are now on the right.
This requires the sets on both sides to be equal.
animations: Position the line (#00FFFF) horizontally at 0 degrees through a point.
Rotate the line (#00FFFF) continuously through 180 degrees.
Fade in labels 'Initial' at 0 deg and 'Final' at 180 deg.
Shift the color of points from Cyan (#00FFFF) to Magenta (#FF00FF) as they cross sides.
Highlight the final 180-degree state with a pulse effect.

sections.title: Conclusion: Infinite Connectivity
lecture_lines: The invariant forces the line to visit every point.
Each point eventually serves as the windmill's pivot.
Geometry and combinatorics unite to reveal this elegant pattern.
animations: Speed up the rotation of the windmill [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/windmill.svg] through multiple points to show the 'Dance'.
Draw the connection path (#FFFF00) formed by the pivots.
Fade out all elements except the final connected path.
